searchLog: Read life/PIPELINE.md, life/PROFILE.md, life/OUTLOOK.md section 5, profile.md, and data/target-companies.json before hunting. Independently re-verified today's root-cause claim rather than trusting the prior day's log: tried WebFetch on job-boards.greenhouse.io/xai, api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/cursor, www.databricks.com, openai.com, and www.startupschool.org -- all five returned getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND (session network allowlist denial, not a transient fault). www.anthropic.com/careers/jobs DID resolve and loaded; its visible listings are Forward Deployed Engineer (exp required), ~30 Applied AI Architect variants (exp required), Technical Program Manager (all specialized/senior), and early-career-shaped titles (Research Associate, Product Support Specialist, Research Resident, Fellows Program) -- none a new new-grad posting since the last check, and the actual Greenhouse apply pages linked from it are themselves unreachable, so even Anthropic's listings can't be verified against hunt.md's 'fetch the real apply page' bar. No candidate cleared verification. 0 verified is the correct, honest result today.
knownIssue: CONFIRMED AGAIN, independently, 2026-11-15: this cloud session's network egress allowlist blocks nearly every external domain except www.anthropic.com. This is not a job-board-specific gap -- openai.com and startupschool.org (unrelated to Greenhouse/Ashby) also failed to resolve. At least 10 prior daily runs (2026-10-26 through 2026-11-14, per git log on data/hunt-results.json) found and logged the same root cause, several explicitly claiming to escalate via PushNotification each time -- but life/LOG.md and life/TODO.md (where a durable fact like this should land per the hub's own rule 4) show no trace it was ever recorded, and this routine is read-only on life/ so it cannot write the escalation there itself. This run sent an actual PushNotification making the ask explicit, rather than only logging an intent to. Until the session/routine's network allowlist is widened, this routine can structurally never produce a verified opportunity -- 0-verified days since late July/August are indistinguishable from 'no good opportunities' in the email, which is the exact failure mode this field exists to flag.
